project.name: Lumen Desk
project.tagline: A made-up help desk product used as the sample map: customers ask questions in a widget, agents answer from an inbox with AI-drafted replies.
project.summary: A web app and an embeddable widget in front of one API server and a Postgres database. AI replies run through a single assistant endpoint that calls a hosted model. Payments and email go through outside providers.

starters: How does a customer question reach an agent?
Where does AI run, and what can it look up?
What happens when a team upgrades its plan?
What can an admin do that an agent cannot?

nodes.label: Help Widget
nodes.detail: A small form customers open from the product's own website. It collects an email address and a question and posts them to the API.
nodes.why: The front door for every customer question.

nodes.label: Agent Inbox
nodes.detail: Where support agents see open tickets, read the conversation, ask for a suggested reply, answer and close.
nodes.why: The screen agents work in all day.

nodes.label: Sign-in
nodes.detail: Email and password sign-in for agents and admins.
nodes.why: Keeps customer conversations private to the team.

nodes.label: Billing page
nodes.detail: Shows the current plan and seat count. Admins start a checkout to change either.
nodes.why: Self-serve upgrades.

nodes.label: Payment Webhook
nodes.detail: Receives payment and subscription events, verifies the signature and updates the team's plan.
nodes.why: The plan a team sees always matches what it paid for.

nodes.label: Daily Digest Job
nodes.detail: Each morning it finds tickets that have waited more than a day and queues one summary email per agent.
nodes.why: Nothing sits unanswered without someone being told.

nodes.label: Session Service
nodes.detail: Checks the session on every request and loads the user's team and role.
nodes.why: One place decides who is allowed in.

nodes.label: Ticket Service
nodes.detail: Creates tickets from the widget, stores every message, assigns an owner and closes tickets. Asks the triage agent to label each new ticket.
nodes.why: The core record of every customer conversation.

nodes.label: Reply Assistant API
nodes.detail: The only endpoint that talks to the model. It loads the conversation, runs the suggestion prompt and returns a draft. The API key stays on the server.
nodes.why: Keeps AI in one reviewable place.

nodes.label: Billing Service
nodes.detail: Reads the team's plan and opens a checkout session with the payment provider.
nodes.why: Turns a plan change into a payment.

nodes.label: Notification Service
nodes.detail: Queues and sends email: replies to customers and the daily digest to agents.
nodes.why: How the product reaches people outside the app.

nodes.label: Reply Suggester
nodes.detail: Drafts a reply from the conversation so far. It may search the help articles first and is told to say when no article covers the question.
nodes.why: Agents start from a draft instead of a blank box.

nodes.label: Ticket Triage
nodes.detail: Labels each new ticket with a topic and an urgency so the inbox can sort it.
nodes.why: Urgent questions rise to the top without anyone reading them first.

nodes.label: Claude Sonnet
nodes.detail: The one model both prompts use.
nodes.why: A single model keeps cost and behaviour predictable.

nodes.label: Search Help Articles
nodes.detail: A tool the reply suggester can call to find help articles that match the question.
nodes.why: Grounds drafts in what the team has already written.

nodes.label: Tickets
nodes.detail: Postgres tables for tickets and their messages, with the topic, urgency, owner and status of each ticket.
nodes.why: The history of every conversation.

nodes.label: Accounts
nodes.detail: Postgres tables for users, teams, roles and each team's plan.
nodes.why: Who is on which team, and what the team pays for.

nodes.label: Help Articles
nodes.detail: Help articles written by the team, with a search index over their text.
nodes.why: The knowledge the AI is allowed to draw on.

nodes.label: Anthropic API
nodes.detail: Hosted model API, reached only from the reply assistant endpoint.
nodes.why: Provides the model.

nodes.label: Payment Provider
nodes.detail: Hosted checkout and subscription billing. Always called from the server.
nodes.why: Takes the money and is the source of truth for plans.

nodes.label: Email Provider
nodes.detail: Delivers every email the product sends.
nodes.why: Reliable delivery without running a mail server.

roles.name: Customer
roles.d: Someone using the product that Lumen Desk supports. They have no account.
roles.can: Send a question through the widget and reply by email.
roles.cannot: See other customers' tickets or sign in.

roles.name: Agent
roles.goals: Clear the inbox with accurate replies.
roles.can: Read, assign, answer and close tickets; ask for AI drafts.
roles.cannot: Change the plan or invite people.

roles.name: Admin
roles.goals: Keep the team staffed and the plan paid.
roles.can: Everything an agent can, plus billing and team settings.
roles.cannot: Nothing inside the team is closed to them.

techStack.summary: A TypeScript codebase end to end: two browser apps, one Node API with a job queue, Postgres and Redis for data, and three outside services for AI, payments and email.

securityReview.summary: Sign-in, tenant scoping and the payment webhook are handled soundly. The main gaps are one missing role check on plan changes and no rate limit on the public widget endpoint.
securityReview.scope: A static, read-only review of the code in this repository, made while mapping it. It is not a penetration test and no running system was touched. Each item cites the file it is based on; items marked as needing a check depend on settings outside the repository.

items.title: Sessions use HTTP-only, signed cookies
items.d: The session service sets the cookie as HTTP-only, secure and same-site, and stores the session server-side.

items.title: Ticket queries are scoped to the account
items.d: Every ticket query adds the signed-in agent's account id on the server, so one team cannot read another team's tickets.

items.title: Plan changes do not re-check the role
items.d: The billing page hides the upgrade button from agents, but the API route that opens checkout only checks that the caller is signed in.
items.impact: Any agent could start a plan change for their team by calling the route directly.
items.fix: Check the admin role in the billing service before opening checkout, and add a test for an agent caller.

items.title: Payment webhook verifies the signature
items.d: The webhook rejects any event whose signature does not match, before reading the body as an event.

items.title: Public widget endpoint has no rate limit
items.d: The endpoint the help widget posts to accepts unlimited requests per visitor and per site.
items.impact: A script could flood a team's inbox with tickets, and each one triggers an AI triage call that costs money.
items.fix: Add a per-site and per-IP limit in front of ticket creation, and cap triage calls per account per hour.

items.title: No Content-Security-Policy is set in code
items.d: The API and web app set no Content-Security-Policy header. It may be added by the hosting proxy, which is not in this repository.
items.impact: Without one, an injected script would run with no restriction on where it can send data.
items.fix: Confirm whether the proxy sets the header; if not, add a policy that allows only the app's own scripts.

items.title: The AI's only tool reads help articles
items.d: The reply suggester can call one tool, which searches published help articles. It cannot write data or reach tickets from other accounts.

items.title: Customer text reaches the prompt unchanged
items.d: The customer's message is placed in the prompt as written. The draft is shown to an agent, who must send it; nothing is sent automatically.
items.impact: A customer could write text that steers the draft. The agent review step limits the effect to a misleading suggestion.
items.fix: Keep the review step mandatory and mark customer text clearly as quoted material in the prompt.

items.title: Digest emails include ticket subjects
items.d: The daily digest lists open ticket subjects in the email body, so that text leaves the system through the email provider.
items.impact: Ticket subjects can contain customer details that then sit in inboxes outside the product.
items.fix: Offer a setting that sends counts only, with a link back to the inbox.

notCovered: Dependency vulnerabilities: no audit was run.
Settings held outside the repository, such as proxy headers and provider dashboards.
Behaviour of the running system under load or attack.
